S2. Variable description

Distributional characteristics of the scores used

dat$Cognitive_sss <- rowSums(dat[, c("stigma_auto_1", "stigma_auto_2", "stigma_auto_3")])
dat$Affective_sss <- rowSums(dat[, c("stigma_auto_4", "stigma_auto_5", "stigma_auto_6")])
dat$Behavioural_sss <- rowSums(dat[, c("stigma_auto_7", "stigma_auto_8", "stigma_auto_9")])

vars <- c("Cognitive_sss", "Affective_sss", "Behavioural_sss")


# -----------------------------
# 2) Data-visualisation globale avec dfSummary (mini histogrammes + NA, etc.)
# -----------------------------
dfs <- dfSummary(
  dat[vars],
  style      = "grid",
  graph.col  = TRUE,   # mini-graphiques dans la colonne Graph
  valid.col  = TRUE,
  na.col     = TRUE
)


# ou rendu console / HTML
print(dfs, method = "render")

CFA comparison

The weak contribution of items 4 and 7 may reflect participants’ treatment appraisal and illness understanding, possibly linked to care engagement, psychotherapy exposure, repeated depressive episodes, or contact with specialized mental health care, rather than item misinterpretation.

# alternative model 1

cfa_model_multi <- '
F1 =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8
F2 =~ item3 + item4 + item7
'

fit_multi_bipq1 <- cfa(
  cfa_model_multi,
  data = data_efa_bipq,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = paste0("item", c(1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8))
)

summary(
  fit_multi_bipq1,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE,
  rsquare = TRUE
)

Both previously reported two-factor B-IPQ models yielded inadmissible solutions under WLSMV estimation, with negative residual variances for item 3 (−2.416 and −2.789 for the first and second models, respectively) and standardised factor loadings exceeding 1 (1.848 and 1.947, respectively). Sensitivity analyses using MLR yielded the same estimation issue, with negative residual variances for item 3 (−6.754 and −6.962, respectively) and standardised loadings of 1.450 and 1.461, respectively.

CFA comparison

# Two-factor correlated model
cfa_model_phq_2f <- '
Somatic =~ item3 + item4 + item5 + item8

CognitiveAffective =~ item1 + item2 + item6 + item7 + item9

Somatic ~~ CognitiveAffective
'

fit_phq_2f <- cfa(
  cfa_model_phq_2f,
  data = data_efa_phq,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = items_phq
)

# Model summary
summary(

Bifactor model

# Bifactor model
cfa_model_phq_bifactor <- '
# General factor
General =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5 +
           item6 + item7 + item8 + item9

# Specific factors
Somatic =~ item3 + item4 + item5 + item8

CognitiveAffective =~ item1 + item2 + item6 + item7 + item9

# Orthogonal factors
General ~~ 0*Somatic
General ~~ 0*CognitiveAffective
Somatic ~~ 0*CognitiveAffective
'

fit_phq_bifactor <- cfa(
  cfa_model_phq_bifactor,
  data = data_efa_phq,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = items_phq,
  std.lv = TRUE
)

# Model summary
summary(
  fit_phq_bifactor,
  fit.measures = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE,
  rsquare = TRUE
)

Supplementary bifactorial indices

# 1. Extraire les saturations factorielles standardisées
L <- inspect(fit_phq_bifactor, "std")$lambda

# Vérifier la structure
print(L)
##       Generl Somatc CgntvA
## item1  0.691  0.000  0.359
## item2  0.719  0.000  0.580
## item3  0.581  0.460  0.000
## item4  0.711  0.316  0.000
## item5  0.619  0.193  0.000
## item6  0.651  0.000  0.282
## item7  0.767  0.000 -0.162
## item8  0.578 -0.030  0.000
## item9  0.593  0.000  0.377
# 2. Extraire les variances résiduelles standardisées
theta <- diag(inspect(fit_phq_bifactor, "std")$theta)

# 3. Saturations sur les trois facteurs
g <- L[, "General"]
s <- L[, "Somatic"]
c <- L[, "CognitiveAffective"]

# 4. Explained Common Variance (ECV)
ECV <- sum(g^2) / sum(L^2)

# 5. Omega total (omega)
variance_totale_commune <- sum(colSums(L)^2)
variance_erreur <- sum(theta)

omega <- variance_totale_commune /
  (variance_totale_commune + variance_erreur)

# 6. Omega hiérarchique (omega H)
omegaH <- sum(g)^2 /
  (variance_totale_commune + variance_erreur)

# 7. Afficher les résultats
data.frame(
  Index = c("Omega total", "Omega hierarchical", "ECV"),
  Value = round(c(omega, omegaH, ECV), 3)
)
##                Index Value
## 1        Omega total 0.904
## 2 Omega hierarchical 0.834
## 3                ECV 0.787

        item5 + item6 + item7 + item8 + item9

)

Bifactor model

cfa_model_sss_bifactor <- '
# General factor
General =~ item1 + item2 + item3 + item4 + item5 +
           item6 + item7 + item8 + item9

# Specific factors
  Cognitive =~ item1 + item2 + item3
  Affective =~ item4 + item5 + item6
  Behavioural =~ item7 + item8 + item9

 # Orthogonality between general and specific factors
  General ~~ 0*Cognitive
  General ~~ 0*Affective
  General ~~ 0*Behavioural

  # Orthogonality between specific factors
  Cognitive ~~ 0*Affective
  Cognitive ~~ 0*Behavioural
  Affective ~~ 0*Behavioural
'

fit_sss_bifactor <- cfa(
  cfa_model_sss_bifactor,
  data = data_efa_sss,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  ordered = items_sss,
  std.lv = TRUE
)

# Test de Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin
KMO(cor_all)
## Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin factor adequacy
## Call: KMO(r = cor_all)
## Overall MSA =  0.89
## MSA for each item = 
## stigma_auto_1 stigma_auto_2 stigma_auto_3 stigma_auto_4 stigma_auto_5 
##          0.86          0.93          0.94          0.91          0.89

##  Stigma_ext_2  Stigma_ext_3  Stigma_ext_4  Stigma_ext_5 
##          0.87          0.84          0.91          0.83
# Test de sphéricité de Bartlett
cortest.bartlett(
  cor_all,
  n = nrow(items_all)
)

CFA comparaison 1 ou 2 facteurs corrélés

# -------------------------
# Modèle à 1 facteur
# -------------------------
items_all <- c(
  "stigma_auto_1",
  "stigma_auto_2",
  "stigma_auto_3",
  "stigma_auto_4",
  "stigma_auto_5",
  "stigma_auto_6",
  "stigma_auto_7",
  "stigma_auto_8",
  "stigma_auto_9",
  "Stigma_ext_1",
  "Stigma_ext_2",
  "Stigma_ext_3",
  "Stigma_ext_4",
  "Stigma_ext_5"
)
model_1f <- '
Stigma =~ stigma_auto_1 + stigma_auto_2 + stigma_auto_3 +
          stigma_auto_4 + stigma_auto_5 + stigma_auto_6 +
          stigma_auto_7 + stigma_auto_8 + stigma_auto_9 +
          Stigma_ext_1 + Stigma_ext_2 + Stigma_ext_3 +
          Stigma_ext_4 + Stigma_ext_5
'

fit_1f <- cfa(
  model_1f,
  data = dat_stigma,
  ordered = items_all,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  std.lv = TRUE
)

# -------------------------
# Modèle à 2 facteurs corrélés
# -------------------------

model_2f <- '
SelfStigma =~ stigma_auto_1 + stigma_auto_2 + stigma_auto_3 +
             stigma_auto_4 + stigma_auto_5 + stigma_auto_6 +
             stigma_auto_7 + stigma_auto_8 + stigma_auto_9

ExternalStigma =~ Stigma_ext_1 + Stigma_ext_2 + Stigma_ext_3 +
                  Stigma_ext_4 + Stigma_ext_5
'

fit_2f <- cfa(
  model_2f,
  data = dat_stigma,
  ordered = items_all,
  estimator = "WLSMV",
  std.lv = TRUE
)

rbind(
  "1 facteur" = fitMeasures(
    fit_1f,
    c(
      "cfi.robust",
      "rmsea.robust",
      "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
      "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
      "srmr"
    )
  ),
  "2 facteurs" = fitMeasures(
    fit_2f,
    c(
      "cfi.robust",
      "rmsea.robust",
      "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
      "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
      "srmr"
    )
  )
)
##            cfi.robust rmsea.robust rmsea.ci.lower.robust rmsea.ci.upper.robust
## 1 facteur   0.7040890    0.1658338             0.1604837             0.1712455
## 2 facteurs  0.7210964    0.1620534             0.1561707             0.1680116
##                  srmr
## 1 facteur  0.11617297
## 2 facteurs 0.09698591
lavTestLRT(fit_1f, fit_2f)
## 
## Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = "satorra.2000")
## 
## lavaan->lavTestLRT():  
##    lavaan NOTE: The "Chisq" column contains standard test statistics, not the 
##    robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference test is 
##    a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.
## 
##        Df AIC BIC  Chisq Chisq diff   RMSEA Df diff Pr(>Chisq)    
## fit_2f 76         2321.2                                          
## fit_1f 77         2764.5     280.32 0.40246       1  < 2.2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
pe <- parameterEstimates(
  fit_2f,
  ci = TRUE,
  standardized = TRUE
)

pe[
  pe$lhs == "SelfStigma" &
  pe$op == "~~" &
  pe$rhs == "ExternalStigma",
  c("lhs", "rhs", "est", "ci.lower", "ci.upper", "pvalue")
]
##           lhs            rhs   est ci.lower ci.upper pvalue
## 72 SelfStigma ExternalStigma 0.576    0.534    0.618      0
pe[
  pe$lhs == "ExternalStigma" &
  pe$op == "=~",
  c("rhs", "std.all", "ci.lower", "ci.upper", "pvalue")
]
##             rhs std.all ci.lower ci.upper pvalue

## 12 Stigma_ext_3   0.355    0.293    0.417      0
## 13 Stigma_ext_4   0.591    0.538    0.645      0
## 14 Stigma_ext_5   0.575    0.512    0.638      0

    "cfi.robust",
    "rmsea.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.lower.robust",
    "rmsea.ci.upper.robust",
    "srmr"
  )
)
##            cfi.robust          rmsea.robust rmsea.ci.lower.robust 
##                 0.815                 0.132                 0.126 
## rmsea.ci.upper.robust                  srmr 
##                 0.138                 0.073

S5. Exploratory hypothesis testing

Convergent validity

Simple correlation

dat_bis <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(score_PHQ9, Score_autostigma, Score_BIPQ, Score_whodas, score_GAD7)

cor_spearman2 <- cor(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_PHQ9, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
cor.test(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_PHQ9, method = "spearman")
## 
##  Spearman's rank correlation rho
## 
## data:  dat_bis$Score_BIPQ and dat_bis$score_PHQ9
## S = 1368502974, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true rho is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:
##       rho 
## 0.5968822
cor_spearman3 <- cor(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_GAD7, method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")

cor.test(dat_bis$Score_BIPQ, dat_bis$score_GAD7, method = "spearman")
## 
##  Spearman's rank correlation rho
## 
## data:  dat_bis$Score_BIPQ and dat_bis$score_GAD7
## S = 714919977, p-value < 2.2e-16
## alternative hypothesis: true rho is not equal to 0
## sample estimates:
##       rho 
## 0.3636253

Latent model

BIPQ ~ PHQ9

Freely estimated latent correlations

cfa_model_PHQ <- '
BIPQ =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8 + item3 + item4 + item7 + item2
PHQ9 =~ interet_plaisir + triste_deprime + sommeil + fatigue + appetit + opinion_soi + concentration + activite + consequence_pb
BIPQ ~~ PHQ9'

fit_PHQ <- cfa(cfa_model_PHQ, 
               data = data_phq, 
               estimator = "MLR", 
               std.lv = TRUE,
               missing   = "fiml")

#summary(fit_PHQ, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit_PHQ, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))
##   cfi   tli rmsea  srmr 
## 0.891 0.874 0.072 0.058
# 95% confidence interval for the latent variable correlation
latcorPHQ <- parameterEstimates(fit_PHQ, standardized = TRUE, ci = TRUE)

# Result of interest
subset(latcorPHQ, lhs == "BIPQ" & rhs == "PHQ9" & op == "~~")[, 
        c("est", "ci.lower", "ci.upper", "pvalue")]
##      est ci.lower ci.upper pvalue
## 18 0.671    0.642    0.699      0

Constrained two-factor models (correlation == 0.9)

cfa_PHQ_corr <- '
BIPQ =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8 + item3 + item4 + item7 + item2
PHQ9 =~ interet_plaisir + triste_deprime + sommeil + fatigue + appetit + opinion_soi + concentration + activite + consequence_pb
BIPQ ~~ 0.9*PHQ9
'
fit_PHQ_corr <- cfa(cfa_PHQ_corr,
                    data = data_phq,
                    estimator = "MLR", 
                    std.lv = TRUE,
                    missing   = "fiml")

#summary(fit_PHQ_corr, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit_PHQ_corr, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))
##   cfi   tli rmsea  srmr 
## 0.851 0.830 0.084 0.153

Comparison using scaled chi-square difference tests with the Satorra–Bentler 2010 correction.

lavTestLRT(
  fit_PHQ,
  fit_PHQ_corr,
  method = "satorra.bentler.2010"
)
## 
## Scaled Chi-Squared Difference Test (method = "satorra.bentler.2010")
## 
## lavaan->lavTestLRT():  
##    lavaan NOTE: The "Chisq" column contains standard test statistics, not the 
##    robust test that should be reported per model. A robust difference test is 
##    a function of two standard (not robust) statistics.
## 
##               Df    AIC    BIC  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)    
## fit_PHQ      118 160463 160770 1785.5                                  
## fit_PHQ_corr 119 161061 161363 2385.8     457.28       1  < 2.2e-16 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1

One factor model

BIPQPHQ9 =~ item1 + item5 + item6 + item8 + item3 + item4 + item7 + item2
 + interet_plaisir + triste_deprime + sommeil + fatigue + appetit + opinion_soi + concentration + activite + consequence_pb
'
fit_PHQ_1 <- cfa(cfa_model_PHQ_1, 
                 data = data_phq, 
                 estimator = "MLR", 
                 std.lv = TRUE,
                 missing   = "fiml")

#summary(fit_PHQ_1, fit.measures = TRUE, standardized = TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)
fitMeasures(fit_PHQ_1, c("cfi", "tli", "rmsea", "srmr"))
##   cfi   tli rmsea  srmr 
## 0.752 0.716 0.108 0.075

S6. Incremental validity

With anova

dat_bis <- dat %>%
  dplyr::select(
    age, Sexe, score_PHQ9, Score_autostigma,
    Score_BIPQ, Score_whodas, score_GAD7
  )

dat_clean <- dat_bis[complete.cases(dat_bis), ]

r2 <- function(m) summary(m)$r.squared

model1 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe,
  data = dat_clean
)

model2 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7,
  data = dat_clean
)

model3 <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
  data = dat_clean
)

# ANOVA hiérarchique
anova_results <- anova(model1, model2, model3)

print(anova_results)
## Analysis of Variance Table
## 
## Model 1: Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe
## Model 2: Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7
## Model 3: Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + 
##     Score_BIPQ
##   Res.Df    RSS Df Sum of Sq        F Pr(>F)    
## 1   1886 155771                                 
## 2   1883 108644  3     47127 272.1462 <2e-16 ***
## 3   1882 108634  1        10   0.1754 0.6754    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
##                             Model    R2 Delta_R2
## 1               Step 1: age + sex 0.071       NA
## 2 Step 2: + PHQ-9 + SSS-S + GAD-7 0.352    0.281
## 3                  Step 3: + BIPQ 0.352    0.000
##                             Model         R2     Delta_R2 R2_percent
## 1               Step 1: age + sex 0.07082479           NA       7.08
## 2 Step 2: + PHQ-9 + SSS-S + GAD-7 0.35193742 2.811126e-01      35.19
## 3                  Step 3: + BIPQ 0.35199780 6.037975e-05      35.20
##   Delta_R2_percent
## 1               NA
## 2            28.11
## 3             0.01

with yhat

Commonality analysis

# Modèle final
res_lm <- lm(
  Score_whodas ~ age + Sexe + score_PHQ9 + Score_autostigma + score_GAD7 + Score_BIPQ,
  data = dat_clean
)

# Commonality analysis
res_common <- calc.yhat(res_lm)

# Bootstrap 1000 resamples
boot_out <- boot(
  data = dat_clean,
  statistic = yhat::boot.yhat,
  R = 1000,
  lmOut = res_lm,
  regrout0 = res_common
)

# IC 95% percentile
boot_results <- booteval.yhat(
  res_common,
  boot_out,
  bty = "perc",
  .95,
  3
)

# Results
print(res_common$PredictorMetrics)
